main_text.l: Quòd, daß. Quoniam, dann / darum daß. Quia, die-weil. Quippe, als das. Utpote, als nemlich. / Ver-
bis primorum vel secundorum temporum conveniunt.
Quanquam, Etsi, Tametsi, wiewol. Quando, sinte-
mal. Quandoquidem, dieweil / verbis primorum tem-
porum tantum conveniunt.
Quamvis, wiewol. Licèt, ob schon. Ut, wiewol. Ut,
auff daß. Ne, / daß nicht. Quin, das nicht / Verbis se-
cundorum temporum tantum conveniunt.
Conjunctionum aliæ præponuntur, ut, Nam, quare,
at, ac, aft, nec, si, quin, nisi, sin, seu, sive: Aliæ post-
ponuntur, ut, Quoq; ; q;, enim, autem, verò: Aliæ in-
differenter præponuntur & postponuntur, ut, Ergo,
igitur, itaq;, quoniam, tamen.
Si verbum primi præsentis præcedat, sequens ver-
bum secundi præsentis esse solet: Sin verbum primo-
rum præteritorum præcesserit, sequens verbum in se-
cundo imperfecto plærunq; ponitur: ut, jubeo, ut fa-
cias. Jubebam, jussi, jussêram ut faceres.
Post Rogo, jubeo, facio: efficio, fio, curo, laboro,
tam, quàm, tantus, talis, adeò, tot, sic, ita, ponitur Ut,
non Quòd.
Post metuo, timeo, paveo, vereor, Ut, negat: Ne,
affirmat. Metuo ut Rector veniat, ich fürchte daß der
Rector nit komme. Metuo ne Rector veniat, ich fürchte daß der Rector komme.
Recita figuras Grammaticæ.
Prosthesis est vel literæ vel syllabæ ad vocis prin-
cipium appositio: ut, Gnatus, pro Natus. Tetuli, pro tuli.
Aphæresis est vel literæ vel syllabæ à vocis princi-
pio ablatio: ut, Ruit, pro Eruit. Temnere pro con-
temnere.

page.notes: Mixed German black-letter words (e.g. "wiewol", "dieweil", "fürchte", "Rector", "komme") are set in black letter within the roman text; rendered here in plain type. The German glosses are printed in black letter throughout, so the lines containing them are transcribed from the scan with the German words as read. Header "Latina." is in small capitals. The text runs over the bottom of the page; the last line is the printed end of a word ("excin-") and is not completed on this page. Some words in the German glosses are uncertain and not marked individually, given the poor scan quality of the black-letter forms.
